Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear-end motor vehcile collision with complaints of right knee pain and swelling. This
summary covers two visits. On initial evaluation, the knee showed mild effusion and tenderness along the medial joint
line, consistent with the reported mechanism, while ligamentous stability testing and neurovascular checks were
within normal limits. Imaging was ordered to rule out fracture. Causation of the knee findings relative to this collision is
not yet clear and will be reassessed as more information becomes available. No prior injury to the same area is
known to the patient or documented in the record. Conservative care was provided, including rest, ice, compression,
and a short course of anti-inflammatory medication with home exercises. The patient followed the expected recovery
pattern, and symptoms steadily decreased by the second visit, at which point the plan was to taper care and resume
normal activity as tolerated. Billing records reflect one charge per service with no duplicate or repeated entries.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
